generatedProse.concept-context: In sport and exercise science, being critical is one habit you bring to every piece of evidence. You question what a training study or test claims, engage with its method and data, and name your moves as you analyse the protocol, evaluate the sample, and judge how far the results apply to real athletes. Across a module, that single practice turns reading research into sound coaching and practice decisions.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two sport science students read the same study claiming a training method boosts sprint speed. One notes the result and repeats it in his report. The other brings the three strands together: he questions the claim, sees the group was small and highly trained, weighs it against another trial, and judges the method as promising but not proven for beginners. His report is stronger, because he was critical on purpose rather than in three separate steps.
generatedProse.summary: In sport and exercise science, being critical works best as one habit across your reading. You question a study, engage with its method and data, name your moves, and judge how far the results apply to the athletes you work with. The whole practice, repeated study after study, is what builds sound, evidence-led decisions.

check.body: A student reads a source, questions what it claims, weighs the evidence against another source, and reaches a reasoned judgement of her own. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first programme, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next programme.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next programme, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next programme improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: The whole critical practice at work: the mindset, active engagement, and the language of weighing and judging together.
_items.feedback: Yes. She brought the mindset, engaged actively, and judged with reasons, all in one go.

_items.text: Passive reading, because she used a source in her work.
_items.feedback: Using a source is not passive in itself. She questioned and judged it.

_items.text: Only analysis, because she broke the argument into parts.
_items.feedback: She did more than analyse. She also weighed the evidence and reached a judgement.

_items.text: Fault-finding, because she disagreed with the source.
_items.feedback: Weighing a source and judging it with reasons is not the same as fault-finding.
